title: What Is a D&C (Dilation and Curettage)?
description: What a D&C (uterine curettage) is, what it is for and when it is indicated. Care in Lima with price alternatives.
keyword: what is a d and c
tldr: A procedure to empty the uterus or take a sample of its contents (after a miscarriage, for bleeding or for diagnosis). The specialist decides the indication; results vary from person to person.
bodyHtml:
A procedure to empty the uterus or take a sample of its contents (after a miscarriage, for bleeding or for diagnosis).

How is it done?

Dilation and curettage or aspiration, done vaginally, usually as an outpatient procedure.

When is it indicated?

Incomplete or missed miscarriage, abnormal bleeding or examination of the uterine cavity. The gynecologist decides.

At Cirugía 24 Horas

We operate in Lima with the same team across different clinics, so you can choose the price alternative that fits you. We also care for patients from abroad.

faqs.q: Is a D&C an outpatient procedure?
faqs.a: It depends on the procedure and the clinic; the specialist will tell you after the evaluation.

faqs.q: Who decides whether I need it?
faqs.a: The surgeon, after an evaluation with tests.

title: D&C: How It Is Done Step by Step
description: How a D&C is done step by step: technique, anesthesia and what to expect on the day of the procedure.
keyword: how is a d and c done
tldr: Dilation and curettage or aspiration, done vaginally, usually as an outpatient procedure. It is done under sedation or regional anesthesia. The specialist decides the indication; results vary from person to person.
bodyHtml:
Before

Tests, ultrasound and fasting; stop blood thinners as instructed.

During

Dilation and curettage or aspiration, done vaginally, usually as an outpatient procedure. Sedation or regional anesthesia.

After

Same-day discharge; relative rest and light bleeding for a few days.

faqs.q: How long does the procedure take?
faqs.a: The procedure takes about 15–30 min; recovery takes a few days.

faqs.q: Does it hurt?
faqs.a: You are treated under anesthesia; discomfort afterward is managed with medication.

title: Am I a Candidate for a D&C?
description: Criteria for being a candidate for a D&C: indications, evaluation and when it is recommended.

tldr: Usual candidates: incomplete or missed miscarriage, abnormal bleeding or examination of the uterine cavity. The gynecologist decides. Final candidacy is decided by the surgeon after an evaluation with tests.
bodyHtml:
Am I a candidate for a D&C?

Usual indications

Incomplete or missed miscarriage, abnormal bleeding or examination of the uterine cavity. The gynecologist decides.

The evaluation

It includes a medical history and tests, and sometimes imaging. It does not depend solely on what the patient wants.

faqs.q: Are there alternatives before the procedure?
faqs.a: Medical or expectant management in selected cases; a D&C as indicated.

faqs.q: Does age matter?
faqs.a: Your general health is considered more than age alone.

title: Risks and Complications of a D&C
description: Risks and possible complications of a D&C and how they are reduced with evaluation and follow-up.
tldr: Like any procedure, a D&C has risks: bleeding, infection, uterine perforation and adhesions (uncommon). They are uncommon and are reduced with proper evaluation, careful technique and follow-up. The surgeon explains them at the consultation.
bodyHtml:
Learning about the risks of a D&C is part of a responsible decision.

Possible complications

Bleeding, infection, uterine perforation and adhesions (uncommon).

How they are reduced

A complete pre-operative evaluation, careful technique and close follow-up. The team's experience influences results.

faqs.q: Is it a safe procedure?
faqs.a: It is a common procedure; safety depends on the evaluation, the technique and the follow-up.

faqs.q: What warning signs should I watch for?
faqs.a: Fever, heavy bleeding, severe pain or foul-smelling discharge.

title: Recovery After a D&C
description: What recovery from a D&C is like: timelines, care and return to activity.
tldr: Recovery from a D&C is gradual: same-day discharge; relative rest and light bleeding for a few days. Timelines vary from patient to patient and depend on medical judgment.
bodyHtml:
Recovery from a D&C happens in phases.

What to expect

Same-day discharge; relative rest and light bleeding for a few days.

Care

Avoid sexual intercourse and tampons for the time indicated; attend a follow-up visit.

International patients

Your stay is planned to cover the first check-ups before you return home.

faqs.q: When can I go back to work?
faqs.a: The procedure takes about 15–30 min; recovery takes a few days.

faqs.q: When can I fly back home?
faqs.a: After the first check-ups and with the surgeon's approval.

It addresses the bleeding or completes the emptying of the uterus, and allows a diagnosis.

Your starting condition, the technique, and following the care instructions and check-ups.

Options

Evacuation curettage, diagnostic (biopsy) curettage or aspiration.

How it is chosen

Based on the diagnosis, the severity and the patient's characteristics. The specialist decides the indication; results vary from person to person.

faqs.q: Which technique is best?

Safety

faqs.q: Is anesthesia risky?
